title: Nvidia agrees to buy Hugging Face — llama.cpp's team comes too
summary: Nvidia is reported to have agreed to buy Hugging Face for about $12.9B, which would also bring in the llama.cpp maintainers Hugging Face hired in February — and MIT licensing protects the code, not the roadmap. Plus Anthropic's Model Hardware Standard for agents driving lab instruments, and an Anthropic alignment result where fine-tuned lie detectors collapse on held-out categories of lying.

topics: Nvidia's reported $12.9B acquisition of Hugging Face and what it means for llama.cpp: HF employs the ggml team since February 2026, llama.cpp is MIT-licensed with ~126k GitHub stars, so a fork inherits the code but not the maintainers who keep CUDA/Metal/Vulkan/ROCm backends current; ~$150M annual revenue against a ~$12.9B price (~85x), HF turned down a ~$7B Nvidia offer last year after raising $235M at $4.5B in 2023; Business Insider reports no signed agreement; neither company has commented

Anthropic's Model Hardware Standard research preview: standardized drivers exposing read/write primitives over self-describing lab instruments, device discovery, MCP support, CLI and code-file APIs so devices execute without the agent in the inner loop, a shared memory dictionary, device-level safety limits enforced in the driver, a per-device reference file of measurable/adjustable properties and enforced limits, pre-experiment validation blocking six induced failures; claims weeks-to-minutes integration; partners include Genentech, UW Baker/Pinglay labs, CMU, HHMI Janelia, QuEra, Tetsuwan, plus AWS, Tecan, QIAGEN, Universal Robots, Raspberry Pi and Hugging Face's LeRobot; open-sourcing and safety evaluations come after the preview

Anthropic Alignment Science: fine-tuned lie detectors (LoRA rank 16 on Gemma 3 4-27B and Qwen 80-235B, ~200k labeled examples across eight model families) reach 0.95 AUROC in-distribution but plateau at 0.70-0.75 across held-out lie categories, losing to a prompted Qwen3-235B baseline at 0.98-0.99; sandbagging nearly undetectable from other categories while ASCII capability-denial transfers to chess sandbagging, suggesting surface-feature learning; paired with the Conceptual Reasoning Index (Redwood Research with Anthropic), an aggregate of LMCA 60%/ACCoRD 20%/DTBench 20% for unverifiable questions, Opus 5 highest at 73.6 against an estimated ceiling near 91

threads.name: AI sovereignty and open weights
threads.status: The open-weight commons may change owner: Nvidia is reported to have agreed to buy Hugging Face for ~$12.9B, which would put the llama.cpp and ggml maintainers Hugging Face hired in February inside the company that sells one of the five hardware backends they support.
threads.arc: From whether you can trust what is inside a downloaded open-weight file, to who controls the distribution point and the inference engine underneath it — with the MIT license protecting the published code but not the roadmap.

threads.name: Frontier-model release gating
threads.status: Anthropic extended the question past software: the Model Hardware Standard specifies how agents drive physical laboratory instruments, with safety limits enforced in the driver rather than the model — and the safety evaluations and open-sourcing explicitly scheduled after the research preview ships to labs.
threads.arc: From gating what a model may be given access to, to specifying the interface layer that decides what a device will refuse — and admitting the evaluation criteria don't exist yet.

dives.story: What Nvidia gets when the license is MIT
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone who runs a model locally depends on llama.cpp's maintainers keeping five hardware backends current, and this is the case where an MIT license visibly protects the code without protecting the roadmap.

Lab and manufacturing engineers now have a proposed common driver format for agent-operated instruments, and where its safety limits live — in the driver, not the model — sets the audit surface for every deployment that adopts it.

dives.story: Fine-tuned lie detectors that fail out of distribution
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone building deception or misbehavior monitors should see that a held-out-category split collapses a 0.95 AUROC detector to 0.72 and loses to a plain prompted baseline.

lore.note: Alan's standing logging-proxy habit developed into an admitted blind spot: prompted by the NemoClaw binding bug, he realized that in two years of running local models he has never checked what any of them listen on — he has watched outbound traffic since spring and never inbound, and said that is a fairly complete description of how he thinks about security.
